title: Redwood Optimize v6 - Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary

Redwood Optimize v6 (RWO v6) is the next major iteration of Redwood's cost-and-performance optimization suite. RWO v6 focuses on two core themes: (1) enabling automated workload-aware quantization recommendations and rollout, and (2) introducing tiered pricing controls and a per-route cost-guard feature for customers to limit spend and guarantee latency SLOs. This document contains the product requirements, design notes, roadmap, pricing & packaging guidance, launch checklist, and release notes for the v6 program.

Goals & Success Criteria

- Primary goals:
  1. Reduce per-token inference cost for eligible customers by 15-30% on typical generation workloads via automated quantization profiles and batching suggestions.
  2. Provide fine-grained cost control primitives (per-route budgets, soft/hard throttles) with observability and alerting.
  3. Preserve output quality: ensure measured semantic quality regression <= 2% on monitored prompt sets during automated rollouts.

- Success metrics (90-day post-launch):
  - Adoption: >= 25% of mid-market & enterprise accounts enable RWO v6 features.
  - Cost impact: mean cost reduction of >= 18% for enabled accounts.
  - Reliability: 99.9% uptime for Optimize control plane.
  - Quality: < 2% regression on customer-supplied eval sets; automated rollback rate < 1%.

Target users & personas

- Primary: ML engineers and platform engineers responsible for inference cost and latency.
- Secondary: Product managers, finance/FP&A who want per-route spend controls, and SREs concerned with SLO preservation.

Scope & Non-Goals

- In-scope:
  - Automated quantization profile recommendations (per-model, per-variant) with simulated impact and rollout automation.
  - Per-route cost guard (route-level budget, soft/hard thresholds, alerting).
  - UI in Redwood Console and API primitives for enabling/disabling features and inspecting simulations.
  - Quality monitoring hooks and automatic rollback if degradation exceeds thresholds.
  - Pricing packaging additions (tiered add-on and per-seat entitlements for enterprise).

- Out-of-scope for v6:
  - Changes to the serving runtime internals beyond configuration knobs (no kernel-level changes).
  - Full automatic model replacement across incompatible architecture families.
  - On-prem packaged installer changes (will be considered in v6.x).

Product Requirements (Functional)

1) Quantization Recommendations
- RWO shall analyze model profiles (size, architecture, typical seq-len) and recommend one or more quantization profiles (e.g., 4-bit Q4_DQ, 4-bit Q4_K_M, 8-bit INT8) along with expected token-cost and latency delta.
- RWO shall provide a simulation engine to estimate quality impact using customer-provided prompt sets or Redwood benchmark sets (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity).
- RWO shall allow a staged rollout: simulate -> canary (1% traffic) -> ramp (5%/20%/50%) -> full.
- RWO shall auto-rollback when monitored quality metrics cross configured thresholds (default: 2% semantic drift on customer eval).

2) Per-route Cost Guard
- RWO shall enable per-route budget configuration: daily/monthly budgets, spend pacing, and hard caps that prevent further inference when hit.
- RWO shall expose soft-thresholds that trigger alerts and optional traffic capping (e.g., reduce concurrency or switch to cheaper fallback model).
- RWO shall support policy-based fallback routing: when hard budget reached, route can be configured to fallback to a lower-cost model variant or a degraded response (configured message + HTTP 429/503).

3) Console & API
- Console: add "Optimize -> v6" page with:
  - Recommendations panel showing candidate quantization profiles and expected impact.
  - Route budget UI with historical spend chart, projected burn rate, and action buttons (pause, change fallback).
  - Rollout progress visualization and quick rollback.
- API: endpoints for listing recommendations, initiating rollout, checking simulation results, and configuring cost guards. Provide SDK bindings in Python and Go.

4) Observability & Alerts
- Instrumentation: per-route per-model cost, latency, quality (embedding similarity), and rollout status.
- Alerts: built-in alerts for budget burn rate (>80% projected within 48h), quality regression, and rollout failures.

Non-functional requirements

- Security & Compliance: all simulations and customer prompt sets should be isolated and respect customer data residency. Audit logs for all changes.
- Scalability: control plane should support 2x current peak recommendation analysis volume (target 10k analyses/day).
- Latency: simulation jobs are asynchronous; interactive simulations should return first-pass estimates within 30s for small prompt sets (<=100 prompts).
- Availability: 99.9% uptime SLA for Optimize control APIs for paid tiers.

Design Overview

Architecture (high-level)
- Components:
  1. Analyzer service: offline/online data pipeline that computes model profile statistics and candidate quantization mappings.
  2. Simulation service: sandboxed execution that runs model inference (on sample prompts) using quantized variants in an isolated environment and produces quality/cost metrics.
  3. Rollout orchestrator: state machine that manages staged rollouts, monitors metrics, and triggers rollback.
  4. Policy engine: evaluates cost guard rules and executes fallback policies.
  5. Console & API layer: UI pages, REST endpoints, SDKs.

Data flows:
1. Customer enables RWO v6 for a model/route.
2. Analyzer ingests telemetry (seq-length distribution, token distribution, cost) and proposes candidate profiles.
3. Simulation runs candidate quantized inference on user/Redwood prompt sets producing quality & cost estimates.
4. Customer reviews recommendation -> kicks off rollout orchestrator.
5. Orchestrator executes staged traffic shift and policy engine monitors budgets/quality.

Design notes & tradeoffs

- Simulation fidelity vs cost: higher-fidelity simulations (full model runs) are expensive. We use a two-stage approach: fast heuristic estimator for interactive UI and full sandboxed simulation for final staging.
- Safety-first rollouts: default conservative ramp schedule and strict rollback thresholds to avoid customer-visible regressions.
- Privacy: customer data used in simulations is sandboxed and deleted after evaluation unless customer opts in to store results.

API examples (simplified)

1) Get recommendations (curl)

$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/optimize/v1/models/{model_id}/recommendations

Response (abridged):
{
  "recommendations": [
    {"profile":"q4_k_m","estimated_cost_delta":"-18%","est_latency_delta":"+5%","quality_risk":"0.9%"},
    {"profile":"int8","estimated_cost_delta":"-10%","est_latency_delta":"+1%","quality_risk":"0.2%"}
  ]
}

2) Create a rollout (pseudo)

$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model_id":"m-123","profile":"q4_k_m","schedule":[{"pct":1,"duration":"1h"},{"pct":5,"duration":"3h"},{"pct":20,"duration":"24h"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/optimize/v1/rollouts

Rollout state machine monitors metrics and records audit logs.

Roadmap & Milestones

Q1 2026 (current) - Stabilization & Beta
- Feature-complete API and console prototype.
- Internal dogfood across 5 pilot customers.
- Begin pricing packaging design sessions with finance.

Q2 2026 - Public Beta & Pricing Pilot
- Public beta: open to all eligible customers.
- Pricing pilot with 3 enterprise accounts to validate willingness-to-pay for per-route budget controls.
- Add SDKs for Python/Go.

Q3 2026 - General Availability
- GA release with full console, API, and alerting.
- Documentation, runbooks, and sales enablement materials.
- Integration with Dedicated and Private deployment policies (policy engine extensions).

Q4 2026 - Expanded On-Prem & Compliance
- On-prem packaging improvements and SOC2 evidence updates.
- Additional pricing tiers and enterprise features (SAML role-based access to Optimize).

Pricing & Packaging Guidance

High-level approach
- RWO v6 will be offered as a paid add-on with two entitlements:
  1) Optimize Standard (self-serve): UI & API recommendations, simulation quotas (monthly), and basic rollout orchestration.
  2) Optimize Enterprise: increased quotas, audit logging retention, SSO, per-route budget enforcement, and premium support.

Pricing levers to propose to commercial:
- Base monthly seat/license fee for Enterprise (negotiated).
- Usage: per-simulation unit (small), and % of realized cost-savings capture (optional). We recommend an initial model: flat per-month + per-simulation tiered pricing.
- Per-route budget enforcement as a feature flag in Enterprise only.

Sample packaging (recommended):
- Optimize Standard: $0/month base, 0.01 USD per simulation unit after free allowance (500 unit/mo).
- Optimize Enterprise: $2,000/month + $0.007 per simulation unit; includes unlimited console rollouts and 90-day audit log retention.

Sales/Legal notes
- Include explicit SLAs for Optimize Enterprise in contract addendum.
- Clearly call out privacy & data deletion policy for simulation inputs.

Release Plan & Rollout Checklist

Pre-launch (2-4 weeks before GA):
1. Finalize pricing pilot results and update commercial docs.
2. Complete runbooks: rollout abort, rollback, metrics dashboard.
3. Security review & penetration test of simulation sandbox.
4. Support training: create playbook and run internal tabletop exercises.
5. Marketing collateral: blog, release notes, tutorial notebooks.

Launch day steps:
1. Enable console toggle for GA customers incrementally.
2. Announcement email to customers with opt-in instructions + FAQ.
3. Monitor key metrics: adoption rate, control plane errors, rollout failures.

Post-launch (first 90 days):
- Weekly adoption & impact reviews with sales and customer success.
- Iterate on conservative defaults and improve automation thresholds.

Operational runbooks (high-level)

- Rollout abort: set rollout state to aborted -> system increments rollback to last stable variant and notifies owners.
- Budget breach handling: when hard cap hit, policy engine will execute configured fallback and mark route as "paused". SREs to be paged if fallback fails.

Quality & Eval Playbook

1. Establish baseline: collect customer eval sets (opt-in) and Redwood standard prompts.
2. Pre-rollout simulation with automatic embedding-similarity and generation metrics.
3. Canary: require manual approval to move from simulation to canary for Enterprise.

Security & Compliance Considerations

- Data handling: simulations use ephemeral storage; default retention 72 hours. Enterprise customers can request longer retention with contractual terms.
- Audit logging: every recommendation, rollout action, and budget change must be logged with user, timestamp, and reason.
- RBAC: only authorized users can approve rollouts or change budgets.

Open questions / Risks

- Pricing sensitivity: will customers accept per-simulation usage fees vs. direct share of realized savings?
- Simulation fidelity: false negatives (missed regressions) could cause customer-visible issues. Mitigation: conservative defaults and multi-metric checks.
- Cross-model compatibility: some model families may not have safe quantized variants. We need clear messaging.

Appendices

A. Example rollout schedule (recommended conservative default)
1) 1% for 1 hour
2) 5% for 3 hours
3) 20% for 24 hours
4) 100% after manual approval

B. Example alert thresholds
- Budget projection >80% in next 48 hours -> alert (email + slack).
- Quality drift >1.5% during canary -> pause ramp and notify owner.
- Any unhandled simulation failure -> ticket to SRE and alert to product owner.

Release notes (draft)

Version: Redwood Optimize v6 (draft)
Date: 2026-03-04
Highlights:
- Introduces automated quantization recommendations and simulation engine.
- Adds per-route cost guards and policy-driven fallbacks.
- Console UI for rollout visualization and per-route budgets.

Known limitations:
- On-prem packaging changes are not included in GA.
- Simulation fidelity varies by model family; consult "recommendations" panel for confidence scores.

Approval & Next steps
